description: Climate protection and environmental policy are her central themes; most of her parliamentary interventions have concerned environmental issues. As Green Party president she has defended an ambitious CO2 law and a climate fund, and she is a member of organisations such as Greenpeace, WWF Suisse, Pro Natura, Initiative des Alpes, Bruno Manser Fonds and Verein Klimaschutz Schweiz.

She is a long-standing advocate for the right of asylum and the dignified treatment of migrants. She led the Geneva 'stop bunkers' movement against housing asylum seekers in underground nuclear shelters, and is co-president of the Plateforme sans-papiers and a member of Vivre Ensemble; she has called for preserving Switzerland's tradition of openness.

She has championed cycling and public/rail transport, working for PRO VELO Geneva, serving with the Association transports et environnement (ATE) and as vice-president of OuestRail, and co-chairing campaigns on air-traffic and the environment (CESAR, CARPE).

category: Civil liberties, peace and human rights
description: She co-presided the Swiss civilian-service federation CIVIVA, is a member of the Group for a Switzerland without an Army (GSsA), president of the Society for Threatened Peoples (human-rights NGO), and co-chaired parliamentary groups including the LGBTI group and Switzerland-Armenia and Switzerland-Tibet groups.

She advocates for greater transparency in political and party financing and in parliamentarians' outside income; she tabled a parliamentary initiative requiring members to disclose income from secondary activities and is a member of Transparency International Suisse and Public Eye.
